entries.description: A shivering soldier in torn winter fatigue gear holds a coughing child. He offers a sealed military air-filter crate if you provide 5 days of shelter and clean water.

choices.text: Admit both and administer antibiotics.
choices.outcomeDescription: Corporal Vane hands over the air-filter crate and takes up guard duty by the intake corridor.

choices.text: Trade 4 dried ration packs for the filter without opening the inner blast door.
choices.outcomeDescription: Vane takes the rations with trembling hands and disappears into the blowing black blizzard.

choices.text: Aim rifles through the gun-port and seize the filter by force.
choices.outcomeDescription: The soldier curses your shelter and runs into the sub-zero dark, leaving the dropped crate behind.

entries.description: A frostbitten woman in ritual grey rags knocks frantically. She claims she fled the cult after refusing to poison communal wells with concentrated radium slurry.

choices.text: Strip search for hidden explosives, burn her contaminated rags, and grant refuge.
choices.outcomeDescription: Sister Martha weeps in gratitude and begins tending to the wounded in the medical bay.

choices.text: Lock the blast wheel and ignore the knocking.
choices.outcomeDescription: The knocking stops after twenty minutes. Heavy muffled gunshots echo across the snow at dusk.

entries.description: A wind-burned botanist with an insulated cryo-flask requests emergency heating recharge for frost-sensitive perennial legume roots.

choices.text: Connect the cryo-flask to the shelter's battery bank for 6 hours.
choices.outcomeDescription: The roots survive. Tomas leaves 5 packets of non-hybrid carrot seeds and an agronomy handbook.

choices.text: Confiscate the cryo-flask for your own hydroponics bay and eject the courier.
choices.outcomeDescription: You secure the viable roots, but word of the betrayal spreads quickly to the Allotments.

entries.description: An armed inspector and two wardens in pressure suits demand a 30-liter extraction tithe, brandishing municipal pipeline jurisdiction writs.

choices.text: Surrender 30 liters of purified water.
choices.outcomeDescription: The wardens siphon the water and stamp your hatch with a 30-day non-tampering receipt.

choices.text: Seal the intake vents and declare full bunker isolation.
choices.outcomeDescription: Kaelen spits brine on the periscope optics and threatens total pipeline cutoff.

entries.description: A silent figure wearing pre-war stealth composite armor inserts a verification card into the exterior comm port, requesting the bunker's raw Allocation 12 data log.

choices.text: Transmit scrubbed telemetry files while withholding psychological test logs.
choices.outcomeDescription: The operative accepts the encrypted handshake and deposits a crate of military-grade stimulants.

choices.text: Sever the exterior comm cable and initiate electronic lockdown.
choices.outcomeDescription: The operative tags your coordinates with an active microwave locator beacon before vanishing.

entries.description: An exhausted surgeon carrying a lead-lined surgical kit collapses against the outer steel door. She needs 48 hours of warm rest to treat severe frostbite on her hands.

choices.text: Admit Dr. Chen into the medical bay and provide hot soup and dry clothing.
choices.outcomeDescription: Dr. Chen treats all respiratory and radiation sickness cases across the shelter before departing.

choices.text: Refuse entry due to shelter space and rationing constraints.
choices.outcomeDescription: Her frozen scalpel kit is found near the intake duct the following dawn.

entries.description: A group of blinded pilgrims wearing heavy lead aprons kneel outside the periscope, chanting prayers to the radioactive ash clouds and begging for clean water.

choices.text: Pass 10 liters of filtered water through the decontamination airlock.
choices.outcomeDescription: The pilgrims bless the bunker's foundation stones with charred bone dust and continue south.

choices.text: Trigger the high-decibel perimeter alarms to drive them away.
choices.outcomeDescription: The pilgrims scatter into the toxic mud pools, crying out in pain.

entries.description: A communications technician arrives on an electric snowmobile, offering a high-frequency crystal resonator to listen to the Day 340 global broadcasts.

choices.text: Trade 30x electronic scrap for the crystal resonator.
choices.outcomeDescription: The radio receiver comes alive with crisp carrier signals from coastal monitoring stations.

choices.text: Dismiss the courier and maintain complete radio silence.
choices.outcomeDescription: The technician shakes his head and throttles the snowmobile toward the coastal highway.

entries.description: Three children, the eldest no more than nine, huddle under the shelter's exterior camera housing. They haven't eaten in four days. They don't knock. They just sit and wait.

choices.text: Open the airlock and bring them inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: They eat slowly and say very little. The eldest keeps watch at the corridor hatch all night, out of habit.

choices.text: Push three days of rations through the supply slot and explain you cannot take them in.
choices.outcomeDescription: They eat where they sit. By morning the camera shows the space empty. The ration wrappers remain.

choices.text: Turn on the exterior floodlight so they can see to move, but do not open the door.
choices.outcomeDescription: The light helps. A survivor who saw them through the periscope stops talking to you for three days.

entries.description: A four-person garrison fire team sets up a temporary checkpoint 40 meters from your hatch and demands you register your shelter under the Territorial Security Act, granting them inspection rights.

choices.text: Register the shelter. Submit a partial manifest omitting the medical supply cache.
choices.outcomeDescription: Deckle stamps the registration. The fire team relocates 200 meters east and makes camp.

choices.text: Cite pre-war civilian shelter autonomy statutes and deny entry.
choices.outcomeDescription: Deckle writes something in his field book and leaves without another word. You tighten the outer bolt.

choices.text: Offer Sergeant Deckle 2 fuel cells to 'lose the registration form.'
choices.outcomeDescription: Deckle pockets the cells without looking at you. The checkpoint is gone by noon.

entries.description: A water purification engineer offers to install a secondary ceramic filter bypass on your intake pipe — free of charge. She says the Rebuilder Collective is mapping all shelters' water quality for a post-war census.

choices.text: Grant Petra access to the intake corridor for 3 hours.
choices.outcomeDescription: The filter is installed. Water purity readings improve by 18 points. Petra also logs your census data without asking.

choices.text: Decline. You don't want your shelter location in any database.
choices.outcomeDescription: Petra nods professionally. 'Your choice. The offer stands.' She marks the visit as 'declined' in her tablet.

entries.description: A sun-scarred scavenger arrives with a backpack full of pre-war military hardware: three functioning dosimeters, two gas masks, and one intact geiger counter. She'll trade for any combination of food, medicine, or fuel.

choices.text: Trade 8 days of food rations for all three dosimeters.
choices.outcomeDescription: The dosimeters are calibrated. The hunger margin narrows. The trade was necessary.

choices.text: Trade 3 units of antibiotics for both gas masks and the geiger counter.
choices.outcomeDescription: Kira seals the exchange with a firm handshake. The gas masks are military-grade and still intact.

choices.text: Offer 4 fuel cells for the entire backpack.
choices.outcomeDescription: Kira grins — the first grin you've seen in weeks. She accepts and pockets the cells carefully.

entries.description: A Black Ops field handler requests emergency shelter for a compromised deep-cover asset — someone whose cover identity has been burned. The asset is wounded and cannot travel. You are not told their real name.

choices.text: Admit the asset and treat their wounds. No questions.
choices.outcomeDescription: The asset recovers in three days and leaves without speaking to anyone. Handler Voss leaves an encrypted frequency card.

choices.text: Demand full identity disclosure before granting shelter access.
choices.outcomeDescription: Voss stares at you for five seconds, then withdraws without another word.

entries.description: A garrison supply quartermaster arrives with a signed requisition order for 'emergency fuel reallocation' — 12 cells — citing a breakdown of their primary heating tanker during a winter storm.

choices.text: Surrender 12 fuel cells under the order.
choices.outcomeDescription: Lev signs an IOU for replacement fuel. You've seen these before. They often get honoured. Sometimes.

choices.text: Challenge the order's legality — civilian shelters are exempt under the 1987 Protection Accords.
choices.outcomeDescription: Lev checks his orders. He doesn't have a counter-citation. He leaves empty-handed and frustrated.

choices.text: Offer 4 cells as a voluntary contribution — not under requisition.
choices.outcomeDescription: Lev accepts the compromise. The partial goodwill costs you less than compliance and less than conflict.

entries.description: A pressure-suited infrastructure engineer drives survey stakes into the ground 30 meters from your intake tunnel. He explains he's mapping the aquifer route for a new aqueduct and your tunnel may be in the path.

choices.text: Provide Callan with your tunnel survey blueprints to help the assessment.
choices.outcomeDescription: Callan files a positive cooperation note. The aqueduct decision will now include your shelter's data.

choices.text: Post armed guards at the perimeter and declare the area a hazard zone.
choices.outcomeDescription: Callan retreats. The survey notes 'uncooperative civilian installation' in the margin.

entries.description: Six heavily armed scavengers pound on the outer blast door. They're not attacking — yet. Their leader shouts through the speaker grille that they have information about a Hydro Baron advance on your sector and they want shelter in exchange.

choices.text: Negotiate over the intercom. Accept one person inside to verify the intelligence, weapons secured.
choices.outcomeDescription: The intelligence is real. The advance was rerouted 48 hours earlier, but the warning was worth receiving.

choices.text: Activate the perimeter deterrent system and order them to leave.
choices.outcomeDescription: The band withdraws under the siren. You don't hear the intelligence they were carrying.

choices.text: Admit the full group under strict disarmament protocols.
choices.outcomeDescription: Six additional people strain the ration system for three days. The intelligence changes your patrol routes permanently.

entries.description: A young Ash Sign acolyte with burn-scarred hands delivers a clay census tablet, requesting you inscribe the number of survivors in your shelter for their 'Ash Ledger of the Living.'

choices.text: Inscribe the accurate survivor count.
choices.outcomeDescription: Dren accepts the tablet with both hands and bows before leaving. The ritual feels important to him.

choices.text: Inscribe a false count — half the real number.
choices.outcomeDescription: Dren accepts the count without verifying it. You can't know what the Ash Sign does with accurate population data.

choices.text: Refuse to participate in the Ash Sign census.
choices.outcomeDescription: Dren doesn't argue. He marks the visit 'refused' in the tablet margin with a charred stick.

entries.description: A three-person Rebuilder medic team arrives at the hatch with a portable diagnostic unit. They're offering free radiation sickness screenings to all shelter occupants as part of a continental health assessment.

choices.text: Allow the full team inside for a complete occupant screening.
choices.outcomeDescription: Three survivors are diagnosed with stage-1 chronic radiation sickness. Early identification changes treatment options.

choices.text: Allow screenings only through the airlock, no interior access.
choices.outcomeDescription: The limited screening catches two cases. The medics note the restricted access in their report without comment.

choices.text: Decline. Any unknown team entering the shelter is a security risk.
choices.outcomeDescription: The team leaves without pressure. Two weeks later a survivor develops a fever that could have been caught earlier.

entries.description: An elderly man in a threadbare pre-war uniform stands at the outer camera in -22 degrees without a respirator. He carries nothing. He says only: 'I was stationed here during the original construction. I know this bunker's secondary access.'

choices.text: Admit him and hear what he knows.
choices.outcomeDescription: He talks for two hours. He knows about a second maintenance access that bypasses the blast door — sealed, but functional. He stays, and he earns his place.

choices.text: Interview him through the intercom without opening the door.
choices.outcomeDescription: He describes the access location clearly. When you go looking later, it's exactly where he said. He is gone by the time you check the camera.

entries.description: A courier arrives and hands a lead-shielded canister through the supply slot. There is no manifest, no signature, and no explanation — just a note inside that reads: 'In case of compromise. You'll know when.' The canister contains enough SSKI iodine solution for your entire shelter.

choices.text: Accept the canister and distribute the iodine protocol.
choices.outcomeDescription: The iodine solution is chemically verified by your medic. Standard SSKI, clean. You don't know what you've agreed to.

choices.text: Return the canister through the slot and seal the supply hatch.
choices.outcomeDescription: The courier waits five minutes, picks up the canister, and walks away without looking back.

entries.description: Inspector Nara delivers a formal debt notice: your shelter has drawn 420 liters beyond its permitted allocation since Day 150. The Water Authority is calling in 180 liters of purified water or equivalent value in materials — within 72 hours.

choices.text: Pay the full 180-liter debt immediately.
choices.outcomeDescription: The debt is cleared. Nara files a positive compliance report. Your allocation is reset at standard.

choices.text: Offer the equivalent value in medical supplies and fuel cells.
choices.outcomeDescription: Nara accepts the material substitution after a long pause. The conversion rate is unfavourable, but the debt is recorded as settled.

choices.text: Contest the calculation — your internal logs show a different usage figure.
choices.outcomeDescription: The dispute is logged for arbitration. Nara leaves without collecting anything. The outcome is deferred.

entries.description: Elder Cassia herself arrives at your hatch with a sealed clay urn and a request: allow a consecration ritual at your shelter's foundation stone. In exchange she offers access to the Ash Sign's fallout storm early-warning network — three days' advance notice of incoming ash events.

choices.text: Allow Elder Cassia to conduct the ritual at the exterior foundation marker.
choices.outcomeDescription: Cassia burns the offering outside your hatch. Three days later the ash storm early-warning reaches you 62 hours before the storm arrives.

choices.text: Decline — no religious rituals conducted at shelter infrastructure.
choices.outcomeDescription: Cassia accepts the refusal without anger. The storm early-warning is not offered again.

entries.description: An independent cartographer offers to sell a hand-drawn map of the surrounding 40km, marking every known fallout zone, garrison checkpoint, and passable ice road — current as of seven days ago.

choices.text: Trade 5 days of rations for the map.
choices.outcomeDescription: The map is detailed and accurate. Two patrol routes are immediately adjusted, cutting fallout exposure by 40%.

choices.text: Trade 2 units of antibiotics for the map.
choices.outcomeDescription: Rem accepts and counts the antibiotics twice. The map passes to your planning table.

choices.text: Decline. Your existing routes are sufficient.
choices.outcomeDescription: Rem shrugs and rolls the map back into its oilcloth tube. The information goes elsewhere.

entries.description: A garrison corporal arrives escorting a shackled civilian prisoner — a Rebuilder logistics officer accused of supply sabotage. They need to hold the prisoner in your shelter for 48 hours while their transport vehicle is repaired.

choices.text: Allow the prisoner to be held in your secure storage room under garrison supervision.
choices.outcomeDescription: The prisoner is held in silence for 47 hours. When the transport arrives, the Rebuilder officer is gone. No conversation. No explanation.

choices.text: Refuse. Your shelter is not a garrison detention facility.
choices.outcomeDescription: Arda radios for alternative arrangements and waits in the snow for four hours. Eventually they leave.

choices.text: Grant the prisoner five minutes to speak before deciding.
choices.outcomeDescription: The prisoner says the sabotage charge is fabricated — she was diverting supplies to civilian shelters the garrison had cut off. Arda watches and says nothing. You make your decision knowing.

entries.description: A Rebuilder educator arrives carrying a satchel of teaching materials — printed basic literacy and mathematics workbooks, printed on recycled packaging. She offers to run a daily two-hour class for any shelter children.

choices.text: Admit Agna for a five-day rotating residency.
choices.outcomeDescription: Children attend. Adults start attending after day two. Agna leaves the workbooks and promises to return.

choices.text: Accept the teaching materials but decline the residency.
choices.outcomeDescription: The workbooks go into the common room. Someone starts working through the first pages that evening.

entries.description: A calm young man in clean ritual grey stands at your hatch and asks a single question: 'Is there room for one more in your shelter, or should I continue to the next?'  He has a full radiation dose log strapped to his wrist. He is at 280 mSv accumulated.

choices.text: Admit him. His dose is high but not immediately lethal.
choices.outcomeDescription: Jolen stays and helps with maintenance tasks quietly. His dose log never leaves his wrist. He does not speak about the cult again.

choices.text: Explain that his radiation level is too high for your shelter's contamination protocols.
choices.outcomeDescription: He nods, accepts the explanation, and continues walking south on the ice road.

entries.description: A pipeline engineer arrives to inspect the underground water main that runs 8 meters below your shelter floor. He needs to drill a diagnostic access point. The drilling will make your shelter floor vibrate for six hours and requires you to vacate two lower-level rooms.

choices.text: Permit the inspection. Vacate the two lower rooms for the day.
choices.outcomeDescription: The inspection finds a hairline crack in the main — Sorin patches it, preventing a future contamination event. He owes you the information.

choices.text: Refuse — structural drilling near the shelter foundation is a safety risk.
choices.outcomeDescription: Sorin marks the site as 'denied — structural concern' and files for a mandatory access order instead.

entries.description: Handler Kade offers 48 hours of decrypted garrison radio intercepts in exchange for one week of low-frequency signal logs from your antenna array. No explanation. No context. Just the exchange.

choices.text: Accept the exchange — your antenna logs for their intercepts.
choices.outcomeDescription: The 48 hours of intercepts reveal three garrison supply movements you weren't aware of. You adjust your trade route accordingly.

choices.text: Refuse — handing over antenna logs means handing over your shelter's communication fingerprint.
choices.outcomeDescription: Kade nods once. 'Sound reasoning.' The intelligence offer is withdrawn.

entries.description: A garrison lieutenant arrives at the hatch without her unit. She's in full uniform but has removed her rank insignia. She claims to have defected after receiving orders to destroy a civilian water cache that was feeding four shelters.

choices.text: Admit Lieutenant Orel after a thorough security debrief.
choices.outcomeDescription: Orel's knowledge of garrison patrol routes and supply schedules is significant. She earns her place within a week.

choices.text: Turn her away — you can't verify her story and the garrison risk is too high.
choices.outcomeDescription: Orel accepts the refusal without protest. She pulls her insignia from her pocket, looks at it, and drops it in the snow before walking away.

choices.text: Secretly notify the garrison of Orel's location in exchange for improved standing.
choices.outcomeDescription: A garrison vehicle arrives two hours later. The shelter survivors who watched through the periscope don't speak at dinner.

entries.description: A Rebuilder radio technician asks to install a passive relay node on your antenna mast — it would add your shelter to the Rebuilder continental communications network. The node is small, transparent to your own communications, and would let you receive Rebuilder network broadcasts.

choices.text: Agree to the relay node installation.
choices.outcomeDescription: The node is installed in 40 minutes. Rebuilder network broadcasts begin arriving that evening — weather reports, fallout storm warnings, and supply exchange listings.

choices.text: Decline — the node would mark your shelter's location on the Rebuilder network.
choices.outcomeDescription: Alis accepts the answer calmly. 'Security consideration. Understood.' The offer is noted as declined.

entries.description: A scavenger electronics specialist arrives with a mobile repair kit. She can recalibrate up to three dosimeters, replace battery contacts on geiger counters, and repair one air quality sensor — in exchange for two days of meals and workshop space.

choices.text: Admit Nox and let her service all available instruments.
choices.outcomeDescription: All three dosimeters are recalibrated to ±2% accuracy. The geiger counter comes back from the dead. Two days well spent.

choices.text: Hire Nox for dosimeter recalibration only — one day of meals.
choices.outcomeDescription: The dosimeters read cleanly for the first time in forty days. Nox asks if she can eat before she leaves.

entries.description: A garrison weapons compliance inspector arrives with a two-person audit team. Under the Emergency Civilian Armaments Ordinance they are entitled to inventory all firearms held by civilian shelters. They are calm, professional, and carrying their own rifles.

choices.text: Allow the audit. You have nothing illegal but you dislike the precedent.
choices.outcomeDescription: The audit is completed in 90 minutes. Holt countersigns a 'compliant' certificate and files it. Your weapons are returned.

choices.text: Invoke shelter sovereignty and deny access. You will report the team to the civilian arbitration board.
choices.outcomeDescription: Holt records the refusal and submits it for review. No immediate action is taken. This isn't over.

choices.text: Allow a partial audit of non-essential areas, with sensitive equipment 'under maintenance.'
choices.outcomeDescription: Holt files an 'access limited' note. Not suspicious enough to escalate, not clean enough to forget.

entries.description: A Hydro Baron pipeline maintenance worker crawls to your hatch with a deep laceration across his forearm — a pressure pipe burst during a repair. He's lost significant blood and will not survive the 6-hour walk back to his depot without treatment.

choices.text: Admit Finn, suture the wound, and monitor him for 24 hours.
choices.outcomeDescription: Finn recovers. He returns three days later with a case of water purification tablets and his supervisor's personal thanks.

choices.text: Apply basic pressure bandaging and give him enough food to make the walk.
choices.outcomeDescription: Finn makes it. Whether comfortably or barely, you don't know. He waves from the ice road before disappearing over the ridge.

choices.text: Refuse. Medical supplies are too scarce to spend on non-shelter personnel.
choices.outcomeDescription: Finn does not reach his depot. His body is found by the survey team six days later, three kilometres from your hatch.

entries.description: High Warden Corl and two enforcers demand that your shelter undergo 'radiation purification' — a ritual involving pouring ash slurry into your ventilation intake. He insists this is a spiritual requirement for shelters in the contaminated zone.

choices.text: Refuse firmly. No foreign substance enters the shelter's ventilation under any circumstances.
choices.outcomeDescription: Corl marks your hatch with red chalk and leaves. Your survivors appreciate the refusal. Loudly.

choices.text: Offer a substitute — burn ash paper outside the hatch, which satisfies the 'spiritual' requirement without touching your systems.
choices.outcomeDescription: Corl is not fully satisfied but accepts the token gesture. The chalk mark is not made.

entries.description: A woman's voice comes through on an emergency frequency at 03:00. She identifies herself as a coastal radio operator with a 340-hour archive of survivor testimonies. She asks if your shelter is listening. She doesn't ask for anything else, not yet.

choices.text: Respond. Tell her you're listening.
choices.outcomeDescription: A long pause. Then: 'Good. I'll transmit at 06:00 local. I don't have much time.' This is how the last broadcast begins.

choices.text: Do not respond. Maintain radio silence.
choices.outcomeDescription: MERIDIAN transmits for thirty seconds into silence, then cuts the signal. She will try other frequencies. But your shelter won't be part of what she's building.

entries.description: A scavenger medicine runner arrives breathless, having run seven kilometres through a fallout corridor. She's carrying a sealed case of expired-date potassium iodide tablets and anti-nausea suppressants. The expiry is three years ago. They'll work, mostly.

choices.text: Purchase the case with 4 days of rations.
choices.outcomeDescription: Your medic inspects the tablets. 'Roughly 70% efficacy at this age. Better than nothing by a significant margin.'

choices.text: Decline — expired pharmaceutical efficacy isn't reliable enough for rationing decisions.
choices.outcomeDescription: Cass packs the case back and moves on without complaint. She has three more shelters on her route.

entries.description: Seven civilians stand in a group at your hatch. A garrison corporal stands behind them, clipboard in hand. He announces that these seven have been evicted from a garrison-administered shelter for 'non-compliance with the Allocation Act.' He leaves them there and drives away.

choices.text: Open the hatch and take in all seven.
choices.outcomeDescription: Seven people enter the shelter. The ration ledger is adjusted. The garrison has made your shelter slightly fuller and slightly less theirs.

choices.text: Admit three — the most vulnerable by visible condition.
choices.outcomeDescription: Three people enter. Four watch from outside as the hatch closes. The three inside know who was left.

choices.text: Refuse. Seven additional mouths is not survivable at current ration levels.
choices.outcomeDescription: They stand outside the hatch for two hours. The youngest is approximately four years old. Then they walk north into the fallout zone.

entries.description: A Rebuilder supply convoy driver knocks at your hatch after his lead vehicle breaks down on the ice road 200 metres away. The convoy is carrying winter medical supplies destined for three downstream shelters. He needs shelter tools and workshop space to make the repair.

choices.text: Provide tools, workshop access, and two mechanics for the repair.
choices.outcomeDescription: The convoy is repaired in four hours. Yael leaves a case of anti-nausea medication as thanks. The three downstream shelters get their supplies on time.

choices.text: Loan tools through the supply slot but keep your mechanics inside.
choices.outcomeDescription: The convoy completes the repair in eight hours. Cold and time-consuming, but they manage.

choices.text: Refuse. Your tools and personnel are not available for external operations.
choices.outcomeDescription: Yael radios for alternative support. Help arrives from 80km away after a 14-hour wait. The downstream shelters receive their medical supplies four days late.

entries.description: A young scavenger with a broken leg drags herself to your hatch. She's been crawling for over two kilometres judging by her clothes. She has no ID, no faction marker, nothing. Just a broken leg, a severe head laceration, and the will to keep moving.

choices.text: Bring her inside and treat the leg immediately.
choices.outcomeDescription: She recovers in five days. Her name is Rin. She offers to work scavenging routes in exchange for continued shelter. She is worth keeping.

choices.text: Stabilise the leg and arrange transport to the nearest Rebuilder medic station.
choices.outcomeDescription: She makes it to the medic station. Three weeks later she sends back 2 units of antibiotics through a courier. No note.

entries.description: An envoy in a salt-crusted maritime immersion suit stands in the black thaw mud with an encrypted naval transponder. She brings coordinates for the final Northern Convoy icebreaker extraction on Day 360, demanding verified shelter manifests and 15 liters of pure coolant water.

choices.text: Submit occupant manifest and surrender 3 canisters of clean water for convoy berths.
choices.outcomeDescription: Thorne stamps your shelter token into the naval registry and hands over a VHF rendezvous beacon.

choices.text: Copy the coordinates and broadcast them across Sector 4 unencrypted for all survivors.
choices.outcomeDescription: The frequencies flood with acknowledgement pings from isolated shelters across the entire sector.

choices.text: Decline the convoy. Sector 4 is your home and you will rebuild here.
choices.outcomeDescription: Thorne nods grimly, salutes the periscope lens, and wades back toward the coastal ice road.
